clue.text: Mossad is to capture a monster

indicators.note: capture says the words before it hold the answer inside them, seized across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Israeli intelligence sets out to seize some fearsome creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Mossad' through 'is' into 'to'. Mossad is Israel's intelligence agency, which makes 'capture' read as a mission rather than a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who delights in inflicting cruelty can fairly be called a monster, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Absolutely nothing's insignificant to a serious newspaper — on the contrary

parts.note: the apostrophe-s is taken as a plain letter S
wee means tiny, insignificant

indicators.note: on the contrary turns the order round, so the article and the paper are read backwards

parts.note: the FT, the Financial Times, is a serious broadsheet

explanation.surface: Nothing is too trivial for a highbrow paper; or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the contrary' turns AFT (a + FT) into TFA. The S comes from the 's of 'nothing's' taken literally; Sweet FA (Fanny Adams) is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet FA, short for Sweet Fanny Adams, is British slang for nothing at all.

clue.text: Lord Owen once lost direction in flood

indicators.note: lost says a piece drops out of the name before it

parts.note: David Owen, now a lord, was a doctor and widely known as Dr Owen
E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A politician of old lost his way in a deluge.
explanation.walkthrough: David Owen, a former British Foreign Secretary, trained as a doctor and was called Dr Owen before his peerage; drop E (east).
explanation.definitionFit: To drown land or crops is to flood or submerge them completely, so it is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Young dog is penned and tied up

indicators.note: is penned says the animal is shut inside the enclosing word, like a dog in a pen

parts.note: seed means offspring, the young of a family
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A puppy is shut in its enclosure and tethered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young dog' reads as a puppy, but 'Young' is SEED (offspring) and 'dog' is CUR. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Secured and tied up both mean fastened firmly, as a boat is made fast to its mooring.

clue.text: Foolish princess applies for retirement

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the pieces before it are read in reverse order and backwards

parts.note: Di, Princess Diana, is the usual crossword princess
applies, as in applies paint, means puts

explanation.surface: A silly royal submits her papers to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for retirement' turns the whole run DIPUTS backwards. 'Applies' looks like it means 'submits an application', but it is PUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone lacking sense or good judgement; they are straightforward adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Saatchi's core to artist's keenness

indicators.note: core picks out the central letter of the name before it

parts.note: Damien Hirst is a British artist

explanation.surface: The heart of the Saatchi collection is its passion for an artist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Saatchi was the collector who made Damien Hirst's name, so the surface is apt. The middle letter of the seven in SAATCHI is T.
explanation.definitionFit: A thirst for something is an eager desire, so the word is a figurative synonym for keenness.

clue.text: Synthetic alkaline solution bottled by Bill

indicators.note: bottled by says the solution is held inside the next word as if in a bottle

parts.note: a bill is a printed poster stuck to a wall
lye is a strong alkaline solution, used in soap making

explanation.surface: An artificial chemical is put into bottles by a man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is a poster, a bill pasted up.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyester is a man-made fibre, so it is a synthetic, the noun for an artificial material.

clue.text: Rick or Delia might use one

definitions.text: Rick or Delia might use one

indicators.note: to rick is to wrench or twist, as with a ricked neck, so the following letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A kitchen utensil a celebrity cook such as Rick Stein or Delia Smith might reach for.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick Stein and Delia Smith are British TV cooks, so 'Rick' reads as a name; it is the anagram signal, twisting OR DELIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A dariole is a small cup-shaped mould used for puddings, just what a TV cook would use.

clue.text: Prudish artist foolishly tries to represent Eden?

parts.note: prim means prudish and proper
Tracey Emin is a British artist

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the next word is handled carelessly and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A strait-laced painter makes a silly attempt to portray Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eden' suggests paradise, but it is Anthony Eden, the British head of government 1955-57; the question mark marks a definition by example. 'to represent' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden held the top British government office, so he is one example of a holder of it.

clue.text: Vote to relax prohibition

indicators.note: relax tells us to loosen the letters of the word before it and let them settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A ballot is held to ease a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relax' rearranges the four letters of 'Vote'; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is an authoritative ban or refusal, so it is a noun synonym for a prohibition.

clue.text: Guy has bad time in the mountains

parts.note: a guy is a rope or cord steadying a tent or mast
bad in the sense of unwell, ill
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A man called Guy goes through a rough patch up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man's name but is a guy rope. 'has' and 'in the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordillera is a long chain of mountain ranges, as in the Andes, so it is a collective term for mountains.

clue.text: He brutally punishes habitual drug user

definitions.meaning: one who pelts a victim with rocks as a cruel punishment
slang for someone regularly high on cannabis

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses of the same word: one who throws rocks at an offender, and slang for a regular cannabis smoker.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person who executes or punishes with rocks; the other is slang for a regular dope smoker.

clue.text: Monstrous boy consumed by terrible egotism

indicators.note: consumed by says the boy is swallowed up inside the jumbled letters that follow
terrible signals the letters of the next word are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An awful lad is eaten up by dreadful self-regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles EGOTISM into MISEGOT, and 'consumed by' puts B (boy) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Misbegot, an old form of misbegotten, means illegitimate or contemptible, and so monstrous in an abusive sense.

clue.text: Chap in charge of the house, former 8, with the same way of working

definitions.text: Chap in charge of the house

parts.note: the answer to 8 down is a head of government, and John Major formerly held that office
do, short for ditto, means the same as before
MO, modus operandi, is a way of working

explanation.surface: A butler shares the house with a former premier who works in the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 down is the head of the British government; John Major held the post 1990-97. DO is short for 'ditto'.
explanation.definitionFit: A majordomo is the chief steward of a great household, the man who runs the house.

clue.text: Sick of feminine bias

parts.note: F is the grammatical abbreviation for feminine
to colour a report is to bias it, so colour as a noun can mean slant or bias

explanation.surface: Someone is fed up with prejudice against women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bias' is a noun here matched by COLOUR in the sense of a slant given to an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling off colour means slightly unwell, an everyday idiom for being sick.

clue.text: Abscess's yet to be treated

indicators.note: to be treated says the letters before it still need working on, rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: The boil has yet to receive medical attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Abscess's' is fodder, not a link: S and YET together are rearranged by 'to be treated'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small abscess or inflamed swelling on the edge of an eyelid, so it is a type of abscess.

clue.text: Copper leaves beat

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
ff is the abbreviation for folios, the leaves of a book

explanation.surface: The policeman walks off his patrol route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'beat' set a police scene, but the copper is the metal and 'leaves' are book pages, ff.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuff someone is to strike them with the open hand, so the verb is a synonym for beat.

clue.text: Fashionable pop star showing refinement in manners

parts.note: cult, as in cult film, means fashionable among a devoted following
Midge Ure is a Scottish pop star

explanation.surface: A trendy singer displays polished behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Midge Ure is a Scottish singer known for Ultravox and Band Aid. 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Culture can mean cultivated taste and refinement of mind and manners, a dictionary sense.

clue.text: Recluse's reaction, unfortunately, is to squeeze Helen's front …

indicators.note: to squeeze tells us the jumbled letters press tightly round the next piece
unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters before it are disordered
front picks out the opening letter of the name before it

explanation.surface: A hermit's response, sadly, is to hug the front of Helen, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges REACTION, and 'to squeeze' puts H, the front of 'Helen's', inside. The trailing dots join this to 21 across in a run of cookery jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a religious hermit who lives in seclusion, so a recluse by vocation.

clue.text: Tries cutting top off with a wide-bladed tool

indicators.note: cutting top off says the first letter is removed, the top in a down entry

parts.note: having a whack at something is having a try, so whacks means tries
A as written, then W, the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to lop off the top with a broad-bladed implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting top off' drops W from WHACKS, leaving HACKS. 'wide' looks part of 'wide-bladed' but is W, a wide being a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a saw with a fine-toothed blade, so it is a kind of bladed tool.

clue.text: Doctor initially checked her toe and foot

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the following letters are altered
initially picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A physician first examined her toe and then her foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a medic but is a verb rearranging C (first of 'checked') plus HER TOE. 'foot' is a metrical foot; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trochee is a metrical foot of one stressed then one unstressed syllable, so poetry's sense of foot.

clue.text: The Speaker et al suppress revolutionary threat to the House

indicators.note: suppress means press down on, so in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: the speaker together with others refers to themselves as we
a Trot is a Trotskyist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: Parliament's Speaker and colleagues crush a radical menace to the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Speaker' and 'the House' suggest Parliament, but the speaker is anyone saying 'we', and the house is a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet rot is a fungal decay of damp timber, so it is a threat to any house.

clue.text: … or maybe Nigella's boobs

definitions.meaning: nigella, love-in-a-mist, is a flowering garden plant, so several of them are flowering plants
boobs here are blunders, foolish mistakes

explanation.walkthrough: The dots join 17 across, so 'Nigella' suggests the TV cook, but nigella is the plant love-in-a-mist: a flowering plant. 'boobs' means gaffes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that flower are bloomers, and a bloomer is also British slang for a silly mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Work scored for performances in church

indicators.note: work, as a verb, means knead or rework, so the following word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Music is composed for services sung in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work scored' reads as a piece of music, but 'Work' is a verb rearranging SCORED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Credo is the creed sung or recited in the Mass, so its renditions are performances in church.

clue.text: Group of Seven Treaty is a memorable occurrence!

indicators.note: Group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A treaty agreed by the G7 nations is a historic moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'is', which is a link word joining wordplay to definition, so the definition is 'a memorable occurrence'.
explanation.definitionFit: An event can mean a notable or important happening, so it is a noun synonym.

clue.text: Dour, but without bile?

definitions.meaning: bile was one of the four bodily fluids of old medicine, so lacking it is a playful reading

explanation.walkthrough: Medieval medicine held the body ran on four 'humours', bile among them; the question mark flags this whimsical second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dour lacks any sense of fun, and the word also playfully means lacking one of the four bodily fluids.

clue.text: Authentic beach huts are regularly let out

indicators.note: are regularly let out says every other letter is dropped from the words before, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: Genuine seaside cabins are rented to holidaymakers on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop B, A, H, U, S, the first, third and later odd letters of 'beach huts', and the even letters remain. 'Let out' looks like renting, which suits beach huts.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loanword meaning genuine or real, used in English to mean authentic.

clue.text: Is sorry about losing rod and waders

indicators.note: losing says a piece is taken away from what comes before it

parts.note: to regret something is to be sorry about it, so this phrase means regrets
R is an abbreviation for rod, the old unit of length

explanation.surface: An angler apologises for dropping his fishing rod and his boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rod' and 'waders' set up a fishing scene, but the waders are birds and rod is the unit of length, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are long-legged herons that feed in shallow water, so they are wading birds, waders.

clue.text: Sharp blow requires chap to produce bandage

parts.note: a swat is a sharp slap or blow
a chap is a man, he

explanation.surface: A hard smack means the fellow needs a dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' and 'to produce' are link words joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap in strips of cloth, and as a noun it is a wrapping or bandage.
